title.narrative: GreenLinks – Sustainable Horticulture Hubs for a Premium Market Parties

description.narrative: The GreenLinks project strengthens Kenya’s horticulture sector by connecting small and mediumsized farmers in peri-urban Nairobi (Kikuyu, Thika and Kajiado) to premium domestic and export markets through improved production, aggregation, ‘certification’, and retail integration. Responding to rising consumer demand for safe, traceable vegetables, GreenLinks introduces Dutch innovations and local partnerships that make sustainable production both feasible and profitable. The project combines new Dutch technologies and expertise: precision irrigation advisory, lowcost crop monitoring, advanced biological pest control, and hybrid seed varieties—with practical farmer training in Good Agricultural Practices (GAP), Integrated Pest Management (IPM), and post-harvest handling. Three collection centers will function as hubs for quality control, training, and aggregation. In addition, each collection center will host a small input shop where farmers can conveniently purchase inputs and hardware, ensuring timely access to high-quality inputs aligned with the project’s production standards. Through partnerships with Greenspoon and other retailers, farmers will access premium markets offering 20–40 percent higher farm-gate prices. GreenLinks directly benefits 300 farmers, 100 farm workers, 100 youth employees, and several SMEs in input supply, logistics, and retail. Youth will receive technical and business training for employment in farm operations, packaging, quality control, and advisory services—creating dignified, long-term jobs. More end-consumers gain access to pesticide-safe vegetables that improve public health outcomes. In parallel, the project will conduct an export readiness study focused on future trade with Europe, assessing what Kenyan farmers need to meet EU food-safety, traceability, and certification standards and explore financial services for farmers. By embedding innovation, training, and certification into Kenya’s value chain, GreenLinks builds a sustainable business model that endures beyond the project period
